messages:
anna: FYI after v1.12.3 SDKs shipped were seeing routing attribution mismatches in the console. requests show route=preferred but quota is charged to fallback pool.

mike: can you share a minimal repro request/headers? suspect header normalization.

anna: repro curl:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \ 
  -H 'X-Route: preferred' \ 
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

sophia: console traces show routehint=preferred but ledger increments fallback pool id. span id r-3b9f.

raj: digging into spans: the new TS shim lowercases header keys before proxying. our router does an exact-case lookup for X-Route fast-path. that would explain it.

tim: we added canonicalization to reduce dup headers. router fast-path using case-sensitive map was an oversight.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: tolerant-router-match -> canary (5 instances) by raj at 6173001350

mike: mitigation steps: (1) revert SDK canonicalization in next patch (py/ts) (2) make gateway lookup case-insensitive and emit metric for mismatches (3) add console tile to surface tenant mismatches.

sophia: agree. I'll design a console tile: columns tenant | expected_route | charged_pool | mismatch_count (24h). alert if mismatch_rate > 0.5%.

raj: I'll implement tolerant match and add metric routing.header_case_mismatch. will include unit test and small migration note.

anna: I'll cut the py SDK revert PR and changelog note. need owner to cut TS patch as well.

mike: i'll own the TS patch release. after SDKs are out we should announce in release notes about header canonicalization behavior.

tim: long-term: update policy matcher tests to be header-casing-agnostic and add integration test exercising SDKs + gateway + console mapping.

anna: TL;DR plan: revert SDK header canonicalization -> release patches within 4h; deploy gateway tolerant match canary now; add metric + console tile; observe 24h. tagging @mike @sophia @raj @tim

mike: sounds good. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
